module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# No powers as partition numbers

There are no partition numbers $a(k)$ of the form $x^m$, with $x,m$ integers $>1$.

*Reference:* [A41](https://oeis.org/A41)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA41

open Nat

/-- The `n`-th partition number. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Fintype.card (Nat.Partition n)

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

--TODO: these were previously proven with `native_decide`,
-- but really, one should rove the recurrence relation and use that
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by
  sorry --this was previously proven using `native_decide`

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by
  sorry --this was previously proven using `native_decide`

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 5 := by
  sorry --this was previously proven using `native_decide`

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 7 := by
  sorry --this was previously proven using `native_decide`

/--
There are no partition numbers $a(k)$ of the form $x^m$, with $x,m$ integers $>1$.
See comment by Zhi-Wei Sun (Dec 02 2013).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem noPowerPartitionNumber : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, ¬IsPerfectPower (a k) := by
  sorry

end OeisA41

sources_consulted: OEIS A000041, including its definition, offset, initial values, and Zhi-Wei Sun’s December 2, 2013 comment; read through the official OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A000/A000041.seq
Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Card.lean and Mathlib/Data/Fintype/OfMap.lean — cardinality and surjective enumeration.
review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. Sun’s source comment states exactly: “Conjecture: No a(n) has the form x^m with m > 1 and x > 1.” The entry still labels this a conjecture. Nat.Partition correctly represents unordered partitions into positive parts, and Nat.IsPerfectPower requires both base and exponent to exceed 1, so a(0) = a(1) = 1 causes no boundary problem. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, independently checked all six test values, evaluated the sequence through index 12, and proved that the main predicate is equivalent to the explicit universally quantified no-powers statement without using any sorry-backed theorem. Direct OEIS pages returned HTTP 403; the official data mirror supplied the source entry.
